data.gender_notes: Raoul is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Rollo, a Norman chief in 10th century France, Raoul means 'Famous Wolf'. The name has roots in the Old Norse word 'hulfr' meaning 'wolf' and 'raðulfr' meaning 'famous'. The name Raoul carries the meaning “Famous Wolf” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Raoul usually hope their child will grow to embody famous wolf and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: ראול
in_hebrew.meaning: הוא שועל גדול או שועל אלוהי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ראול הוא שם עברי שמקורו בשם העברי ר'עאל, שפירושו 'הוא שועל גדול' או 'שועל אלוהי'. השם נגזר מהמילים העבריות 'ר'ע' שפירושו שועל ו'אל' שפירושו אלוהים. השם ראול מופיע בתנ'ך ככינויו של אחד הנביאים.

in_greek.name: Ραούλ
in_greek.meaning: Αυτός είναι ο λύκος του Θεού
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ραούλ είναι η ελληνική μορφή του εβραϊκού ονόματος ר'עאל, που σημαίνει 'Αυτός είναι ο λύκος του Θεού' ή 'λύκος του Θεού'. Το όνομα προέρχεται από τις εβραϊκές λέξεις 'ר'ע' που σημαίνει λύκος και 'אל' που σημαίνει Θεός. Το όνομα Ραούλ χρησιμοποιήθηκε στην αρχαία Εκκλησία και αναφέρεται σε έναν από τους πρώτους χριστιανούς.

in_latin.name: Raoul
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Raoul est forma latina nominis hebraici ר'עאל, quod significat 'Ille est lupus Dei' vel 'lupus Dei'. Nomen derivatur ex verbis hebraicis 'ר'ע' quod significat lupum et 'אל' quod significat Deum. Nomen Raoul in Ecclesia primitiva adhibitum est et ad unum e primis christianis refertur.

historical_references.context: Raoul I was the eldest son of Otto-William, Count of Burgundy. He became Duke of Burgundy following the death of his father in 1019. Raoul I is known for his involvement in the conflict between the Salian and the Saxon dynasties for the imperial throne. He allied himself with Conrad, the Duke of Swabia, and supported Conrad's claim to the throne. After Conrad's election as King of the Romans in 1024, Raoul I served as his regent in Germany when Conrad was away. However, Conrad's election was not recognized by Emperor Henry II, who supported his own candidate, Henry III. Raoul I died in 1032 and was succeeded by his younger brother, Henry I.

historical_references.context: Raoul de Gaguin was a French nobleman who became the fifth Grand Master of the Knights Templar in 1307. He held this position until his death in 1314. During his tenure, he oversaw the Knights Templar's involvement in the Albigensian Crusade against the Cathars in southern France. He also played a significant role in the Battle of Bannockburn in Scotland in 1314, where the Scottish army led by Robert the Bruce defeated the English army. Raoul de Gaguin was captured during the battle and died in English custody shortly after.
